text:
Alex Chen: Quick sync — proposing a 'staggered sunset' approach for model deprecations to reduce customer friction and operational risk. TL;DR: phase by region -> tier -> opt-in canaries, with explicit pin/exemption paths.

Maya Patel: Sounds sensible. What are the exact gating criteria for each phase? e.g., perf delta, error-rate, and customer opt-out windows?@sales should we include a grace period for enterprise contracts?

Kevin Ortiz: From infra side, we need concrete benchmarks. Proposal: regression <1% on eval suite, generation-quality A/B delta <5% (human-rated), and p95 latency change <15ms for the most common seq len. If any of these breach, auto-roll back.

Nora Li: Legal/comms note — enterprise SLAs may require 60–90 day notice for breaking changes. Also: we need a comms template + migration FAQ for partners. Recommend we map top 20 customers to tiers and flag any contractual blockers before scheduling.

Alex Chen: Agreed. My draft flow:
Phase 0 — Internal canary (redwood infra + internal apps)
Phase 1 — Opt-in external canaries (select 5 customers across tiers)
Phase 2 — Region-staggered rollout (us-east -> eu -> apac) with tiered delay (free/dev: 2w, growth: 4w, enterprise: 8w)
Phase 3 — Grace + forced migration window (if no blockers), then deprecate pinned versions after 90 days.

Maya Patel: For pinned customers: propose an 'exception-lifecycle' where pin is honored for up to 180 days but requires a migration plan submitted within 30 days of sunset announcement. Otherwise we schedule a migration assist.

Kevin Ortiz: Ops notes:
```
rollout_policy: {
  canary_pct: 5,
  ramp: [5, 25, 50, 100],
  metrics: ["p95_latency", "generation_f1", "error_rate"],
  rollback_on: ["error_rate>0.5%", "p95_latency_delta>15ms"]
}
```
We should wire these into the console as enforceable rollout gates.

Nora Li: +1 on gating in console. Also add a customer support playbook: triage steps, escalation matrix, refund/credit triggers. I'll start a draft.

Alex Chen: Customer impact sizing — @Maya can you surface top 10 customers likely to request pin exceptions and their contract windows? We need that to sequence Phase 2.

Maya Patel: Yep — I'll pull that today and share a spreadsheet with columns: customer, tier, contract_end, current_pin, migration_complexity.

ops-bot: Canary job scheduled: model-v4 -> model-v5 in us-east-1 at 1719878400 UTC. Status: queued. :robot_face:

Kevin Ortiz: One more ops ask — add a fallback policy to route requests to a compatible quantized variant when capacity or perf breaches, rather than full rollback. Saves customers from complete outage.

Alex Chen: Love that. We should codify fallback precedence: pinned variant -> fallback-compat -> prior-stable -> error.

Nora Li: Comms note: include a sample customer email that clearly states timelines, rollback guarantees, and migration assistance options. I'll draft and share by EOD.

Alex Chen: Action items:
- Alex: draft the 'staggered sunset' playbook + rollout checklist (due: next Wed)
- Maya: top 10 customer mapping + contract flags (due: EOD today)
- Kevin: perf/regression harness + automate rollback gates in console (POC 1 week)
- Nora: comms + support playbook (first draft 48 hrs)

Maya Patel: :thumbsup: I'll start tagging customers and coordinate with SE.

Kevin Ortiz: I'll kick off perf runs on the weekly bucket and share results in this thread.

Nora Li: Adding legal to loop. If anyone has specific enterprise contract concerns, DM me and I'll escalate.

Alex Chen: Thanks all — we'll reconvene after the initial drafts. If anything urgent pops up ping me or drop in #eng-runtime.
